web.title: Chhakka Phere: Shaadi Dice Kitty Party Game Rules and Twists
web.description: Chhakka Phere is a shaadi season kitty party dice game: roll a six and the jodi takes one phera around a chair. Rules, the bidaai twist, tips and FAQ.
web.intro: Chhakka Phere is a wedding themed dice game for kitty parties where each team has a pretend dulha and dulhan tied by a dupatta, and every time a teammate rolls a six on a steel plate the pair walks one phera around a chair. The first jodi to complete all 7 phere wins for their team. The crazy twist: whenever someone rolls a one, the dulhan must stop and do a 5-second filmy bidaai cry ("Mummy!") before her team may roll again. It needs only a ludo die, a dupatta and a chair per team, so it is a perfect game for a shaadi season kitty.
materials: One steel plate per team to roll the die on
One dupatta per team for the gathbandhan
One chair per team, placed with free space all around it
A phone timer for the 5-second bidaai cry (optional)
steps: Split the ladies into teams of 4 or 5. Give every team a chair in open space, a steel plate and a die.
In each team, pick one dulha and one dulhan. They hold the two ends of a dupatta like a gathbandhan and stand beside the chair.
When the host says "Shuru!", the other ladies in the team take turns rolling the die on the steel plate, one roll each.
Every time a six comes up, the jodi walks one full phera around the chair, still holding the dupatta, while the team counts the phera aloud.
Every time a one comes up, the dulhan must do a 5-second bidaai cry, saying "Mummy!" like in the films, before her team can roll again.
Keep rolling. The first jodi to complete 7 phere wins.
rules: If either lady lets go of the dupatta during a phera, that phera does not count.
If the jodi touches the chair while walking, they must walk that phera again.
A half-hearted bidaai cry costs the team one phera.
The first jodi to finish all 7 phere is the winning jodi.
variations: On a three, the jodi must say one funny shaadi vachan, such as "Main kabhi tumhara phone check nahi karungi", before the next roll.
For the last 3 phere, the dulhan walks in front and the dulha follows, just like the real ritual in many families.
Whenever any team rolls a six, all the other ladies turn into baraatis and do a quick dance before rolling again.
tips: Keep the chairs well apart and the floor clear so the pairs can walk around safely.
Ask the jodi to walk, not run; the speed comes from the dice, not the feet.
Swap the dulha and dulhan roles after each game so more ladies get a turn.
A steel plate makes a loud clang, which adds to the shaadi mood and keeps every roll honest.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Chhakka Phere?
faq.a: It works best for 8 to 20 ladies in teams of 4 or 5. Each team needs a dulha, a dulhan and at least two ladies to roll the die.

faq.q: What do you need to play Chhakka Phere at a kitty party?
faq.a: Each team needs one ludo die, a steel plate, a dupatta and a chair. All of it is already in most homes.

faq.q: How do you win Chhakka Phere?
faq.a: Roll sixes as fast as you can. Each six earns one phera around the chair, and the first jodi to complete 7 phere wins.

faq.q: What happens when you roll a one in Chhakka Phere?
faq.a: The dulhan has to do a 5-second filmy bidaai cry, saying "Mummy!", before her team is allowed to roll again.

faq.q: Is Chhakka Phere a good game for a shaadi theme kitty party?
faq.a: Yes. The gathbandhan, the 7 phere and the bidaai cry make it a natural fit for shaadi season, sangeet or wedding theme kitties, and it is gentle enough for ladies of every age.
